exposure: referral indication (venous thromboembolism, unexplained arterial thrombosis, pregnancy-related morbidity, asymptomatic family members)
family history of VTE in a first-degree relative
VTE risk factors (unprovoked vs. major risk factor-provoked)
outcome: high-risk thrombophilia (homozygous factor V Leiden or prothrombin G20210A mutations, natural anticoagulant deficiencies, antiphospholipid antibody syndrome [APS])
cohort: The cohort consisted of 3550 patients who underwent thrombophilia testing at a tertiary thrombosis clinic, including those with venous thromboembolism, unexplained arterial thrombosis, pregnancy-related morbidity, and asymptomatic family members.
finding: High-risk thrombophilia was most prevalent in women with pregnancy-related morbidity, and specific clinical characteristics such as age <50 years, family history of VTE, no comorbidities, and D-dimer > 500 mug/L were associated with high-risk hereditary thrombophilia in patients with VTE.
